evidence: Cic. Att. 12.1.1: ēgrediēns ē vīllā ante lūcem
Sen. Ep. 13.4: nē sīs miser ante tempus
terms.comment: Like post, with a time or an event: ante cēnam, ante lūcem, ante merīdiem. For a thing, a clause with antequam. For “ago”, see ago.

terms.gloss: a year before, the year before
terms.grammar: phrase: ante as an adverb, with the measure of time in the ablative
evidence: Cic. Sen. 19: annō ante mē cēnsōrem mortuus est
terms.comment: So paucīs ante diēbus, a few days before; paulō ante, a little earlier.

phrases.latin: hoc litterulārum exarāvī ēgrediēns ē vīllā ante lūcem
phrases.english: I scribbled this little note as I left the house before dawn

phrases.latin: sī volēs in convīviō multum bibere cēnāreque libenter, ante cēnam ēstō crūdam quantum volēs ex acētō
phrases.english: if you want to drink a lot at a party and enjoy your dinner, eat as much raw cabbage as you like with vinegar before dinner
don’t be unhappy before it is time

phrases.latin: annō ante mē cēnsōrem mortuus est, novem annīs post meum cōnsulātum
phrases.english: he died the year before I was censor, nine years after my consulship

phrases.latin: atquī tertium, inquit, ante diem scītōte dēcerptam Carthāgine. tam prope ā moerīs habēmus hostem!
phrases.english: “And yet,” he said, “know that this was picked at Carthage the day before yesterday. So close to our walls is the enemy!”

phrases.latin: quam dēlectābat eum dēfectiōnēs sōlis et lūnae multō ante nōbīs praedīcere!
phrases.english: how he loved to predict eclipses of the sun and moon for us long before!
